result_text:
Any folder whose name starts with `mock` or `__mock` is now classified as mock-resources test code, at any depth and with either path separator. The new tests and the existing `SourceFileFilterTest` pass.

**Change** (`codeanalyzer/src/main/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/ScopingConventions.java`, `addTestConventions()`): I replaced the two old rules (`__mock[a-zA-Z0-9_\- ]+/` and `mock[a-zA-Z0-9_\- ]+/`) with one rule, `.*/(__)?mock[^/\\]*/.*`. The `[^/\\]*` part lets the rest of the folder name be any characters, including punctuation and non-ASCII. The match stays within one folder name, so `remock/`, `demo/`, `mock.java` and `mockery.java` are not matched. The existing `mocks/`, `__mocks__/`, `mock-data/`, `mock_data/`, `mock data/` and `mockStore/` cases are covered by the same rule. The other mock rules (`mockapi/`, `Mocks/`, `_mock.*` files) are unchanged.

**Tests:** I added `codeanalyzer/src/test/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/ScopingConventionsTest.java`. It checks the new folder forms, the Windows-style path, and the non-matching cases. `mvn -o -pl codeanalyzer test` for `ScopingConventionsTest` and `SourceFileFilterTest` passed (2 and 6 tests, no failures). Nothing was committed.
